name: bluewater-shorts-07-12
lines: The best fence builder in your town has two photos online.
Both are six years old.
The worst one has forty videos.
Guess who gets the call.
Customers cannot judge a fence. They can only judge what they see.
So film the job. Before. After. Thirty seconds.
No music. No dancing. Just the work.
One video a week is fifty a year.
Your work is already good. Let people see it.
You only need three kinds of video. Your phone can film all of them.
One. The before and after. Ten seconds each, from the same spot.
Two. Answer the question every customer asks. Say your name and your town first.
Three. Show the part nobody sees. The prep. The level. The cleanup.
That last one sells, because it shows what they are paying for.
Keep each one under a minute. Post one a week.
Four things make a job video look good. None of them cost money.
Hold the phone upright.
Stand with the sun behind you.
Wipe the lens on your shirt.
And film across the yard, not down at your boots.
Say your name and your town in the first three seconds.
Add captions. Many people watch with the sound off.
Then ask the customer before you post it.
Your ad report says forty eight thousand people saw your ad.
Great. How many of them called?
If nobody can tell you, nobody is counting.
So count. Ask every new caller one question. How did you find us?
Write it down. Every time.
In thirty days you will know what one new customer cost you.
That is the only number that matters.
An ad is a tap. Turn it on, calls can come. Turn it off, they stop.
But most owners pour that water on the ground.
The ad says patio. The page says everything.
The phone rings. Nobody answers.
The customer looks you up. Three reviews. Old photos.
Ads pour the water. Your page, your phone and your reviews are the bucket.
Fix the bucket first.
Three mistakes eat ad budgets.
One. Boosting a post with no goal. It gets likes. Likes do not pay for trucks.
Two. Changing everything after three days. Ads need a few weeks to settle.
Three. Paying for clicks from two towns over. Set your area to where your crews really go.
And the big one. Never pay for ads you cannot count.
